native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital peaked in the 14th-13th century BCE plateau (BCE 1400/1300, Older Bronze Age, z-sum +4.24), driven mainly by Copper & Gold and Monument Count; Amber contributed least to that peak and instead underpinned an earlier Neolithic capital hump; landscape openness (pollen PC1) correlates weakly negatively and peaks only ~800 BCE, so the social-capital peak precedes maximal openness.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital peaked on the 14th–13th century BCE plateau (1400/1300 BCE, Older Bronze Age), with a z-sum of +4.24, driven mainly by Copper & Gold and Monument Count.
sub_hypo.context: The Older Bronze Age plateau at 1400/1300 BCE in the archaeological capital records.
sub_hypo.relations: Summed social capital reached its peak z-sum of +4.24; Copper & Gold and Monument Count were its main contributors.

sub_hypo.text: Amber contributed least to the Older Bronze Age social-capital peak and instead underpinned an earlier Neolithic capital hump.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of the earlier Neolithic capital hump with the Older Bronze Age peak at 1400/1300 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Amber made the smallest contribution to the Older Bronze Age peak but supported an earlier Neolithic hump in social capital.

sub_hypo.text: Landscape openness, represented by pollen PC1, correlates weakly negatively with summed social capital and peaks only around 800 BCE, after the social-capital peak.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital and pollen records, comparing the social-capital peak at 1400/1300 BCE with maximal landscape openness around 800 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Pollen PC1 has a weak negative correlation with summed social capital. The social-capital peak at 1400/1300 BCE precedes maximal landscape openness around 800 BCE.
